svg.title: The probability simplex is a piece of a sphere
svg.desc: Left: the octant of a sphere of radius 2 that is the simplex of three outcomes in the coordinates 2 times the square root of p, with the great circle through p equal to (0.6, 0.38, 0.02) and q equal to (0.02, 0.38, 0.6) (Fisher-Rao length 1.857), the m-geodesic (1.905), the e-geodesic (1.985) and the chord (1.791). Right: the Hellinger divergence 4(1 minus cos(s/2)) against the Fisher-Rao distance s, starting like s squared over 2 and saturating at 4 for disjoint distributions at s equal to pi.
svg.text: S₂ as an octant of a sphere of radius 2 (ξ = 2√p)
Left: S₂ as the octant ξ = 2√p of a sphere of radius 2 (thin lines: pi = .25, .5, .75). Its Gauss curvature is 1/4 and its area 2π,
both computed in the p chart from the Fisher metric. The Fisher–Rao geodesic is a great circle; the m- and e-geodesics are longer.
Right: the Hellinger divergence is half the squared chord, 4(1 − cos(s/2)), and saturates at 4 when the supports are disjoint.
